ai.description: Günther’s writhing skink reaches 15 cm. It features a cylindrical, bronze-brown body with a pale venter and a distinct dark lateral stripe. It has minute limbs and highly reduced eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Riopa guentheri* is best distinguished by its lack of supranasal scales, a feature that separates it from other similar Indian skinks like *R. punctata*.
ai.habitat: *Riopa guentheri* inhabits moist deciduous forests and leaf litter in the Western Ghats, typically found at low to moderate elevations up to 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Günther’s writhing snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its active hours burrowing through leaf litter and loose soil in search of small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Riopa guentheri* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Riopa guentheri* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, and Kerala at low to moderate elevations.
